WALTER
16″ CLOSED-FRAME DRUM THICKNESS SANDER
WOODWRIGHT PLANFORGE v1.0 · kernel 1.2.1 · WPF-WALTER-16-C
RELEASE: FABRICATION-READY WITH CONDITIONS — not PE-stamped, not UL, not FABRICATION-READY (unconditional).
STOP-WORK UNTIL CLOSED
1. Qualified electrician sizes overload heaters to motor FLA and lands 115 V 20 A, grounding, and the magnetic st
2. First-run commissioning is staged: collector on, hood on, no workpiece, then poplar 0.010″ [T]
3. Verify every catalog number on the live McMaster / supplier page before purchase [S]
4. True the drum OD to 5.000 ±0.010 after glue; do not run an unbalanced blank [T]
5. Track the PVC conveyor empty 60 s then loaded before any oak [T]
6. E-stop blink test: restore power — drum must not auto-restart [T]
7. Do not treat W-sheets, the HTML guidebook, or the Build-app viz as a scaled fabrication drawing — kernel inche
8. Not a permit drawing, not a UL listing, not a substitute for machine-guarding review
RISK CLASS R3
• Powered abrasive drum ~1089 RPM / ~1.4 kSFM with stored rotational energy
• Ingoing nip at drum-to-work and conveyor rollers
• 115 V motor circuit, magnetic starter, E-stop, 24 V feed — electrical [P]
• Kickback / ejection of short stock
• Combustible fine dust; hood and collector are part of the safeguard
• Belt/pulley pinch outboard of the drive wall
• Homemade machine — not UL listed, not OSHA-certified, not PE-stamped
DATUMS
D1 Base top face = Z0. Walls sit on it. Stretchers must not lift a wall.
D2 Drum axis = Z 13.50″, Y 18.00″. Both bearing plates from one story stick.
D3 Idle jack at zero = plates coplanar. True the drum, then jack for parallelism.
D4 Acme nuts clocked together before the HTD belt. Paint a witness mark.
